change.author: Carina Wollendorfer

findings.title: Team admins are rejected: admin check uses && with the owner check
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin` already matches role ADMIN **or** OWNER (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-283). `isTeamOwner` matches OWNER only (:286-295). Joining the two with `&&` makes `isTeamAdminOrOwner` true only for owners. A team ADMIN who is not the organizer or an attendee gets FORBIDDEN, even though the variable name says admins are allowed. Use `isTeamAdmin(...)` alone, or join the two with `||`.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate-attendee checks are case-sensitive
findings.body: The handler lowercases `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` (line 71) but compares it to the raw `guest` (line 77). `Blocked@Example.com`, or a `+alias` of it, gets past the blacklist. The booking flow handles this: it lowercases and runs `extractBaseEmail` before comparing (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:742-743). The existing-attendee check at line 76 is also an exact string match, so `Alice@x.com` is inserted as a second attendee next to `alice@x.com` and gets emailed again. Normalize the email (lowercase plus `extractBaseEmail`, as handleNewBooking does) before both comparisons.

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore the event type's disable-standard-emails settings
findings.body: The sibling `sendLocationChangeEmails` takes `eventTypeMetadata` and skips host and attendee emails when `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` say to (email-manager.ts:495-521). `sendAddGuestsEmails` has no such parameter, and the handler never passes `booking.eventType.metadata`. Event types that turned standard emails off (for example because a workflow sends them instead) still email the organizer, team members and every attendee when guests are added. Add the metadata parameter and the same guards, and pass the metadata from addGuests.handler.ts:168.

findings.title: Emails are keyed on the raw `guests` input, not on the guests actually added
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered input. A submitted address that was already an attendee, and so was filtered out at line 76, still matches `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (email-manager.ts:541). That existing attendee gets a fresh 'scheduled' confirmation instead of the 'guests added' notice. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Sender name uses APP_NAME instead of EMAIL_FROM_NAME
findings.body: The template this one copies, `OrganizerLocationChangeEmail`, sends `from: ${EMAIL_FROM_NAME} <...>` (organizer-location-change-email.ts:1,23). Using `APP_NAME` here ignores a self-hoster's configured sender name, so this one email shows a different From name from the rest of the booking emails. Import and use `EMAIL_FROM_NAME`.

findings.title: Validation error stays visible after success or when the dialog is dismissed
findings.body: Only the Cancel button resets `isInvalidEmail` (line 91). `onSuccess` (lines 36-41) does not reset it. Neither does closing the dialog with Esc or an overlay click (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, line 61), and neither does editing the inputs. After one invalid attempt, the message 'Emails must be unique and valid' stays on screen while the user fixes the input, after a successful add, and when the dialog is reopened. Closing with Esc or the overlay also keeps the typed emails. Reset both pieces of state in `onSuccess` and whenever the dialog closes, and clear the error when the value changes.

findings.title: Error fallback is unreachable and raw tRPC codes are shown
findings.body: `message` is a template literal that always contains at least `undefined: ...`, so it is never falsy and `t("unable_to_add_guests")` is never used. Users see strings like `BAD_REQUEST: Emails must be unique and valid`. Consider showing `t(err.message)`, falling back to `t("unable_to_add_guests")` when that is empty.

findings.title: Should any attendee be able to add arbitrary guests to someone else's booking?
findings.body: Being an attendee whose email matches the session user is enough to pass the permission check. That attendee can then add any number of addresses (the schema at addGuests.schema.ts:5 has no limit). Each added address gets a calendar invite and email sent in the organizer's name, and the organizer's calendar event is changed. `editLocation` goes through `bookingsProcedure` instead (_router.tsx:62). Is attendee access intended here? If it is, should there be a cap on how many guests can be added per request?

findings.title: New guests get an empty name and the organizer's time zone
findings.body: Each guest is stored with `name: ""` and the organizer's `timeZone` and `locale`. Their 'scheduled' email greets them with an empty name and shows times in the organizer's zone. When the first attendee is one of these guests, `attendees[0].name` in the organizer subject is empty too. Consider defaulting the name to the email's local part, as other guest flows do.

findings.title: packages/ui file imports from its own barrel
findings.body: `MultiEmail` imports `Button`, `EmailField`, `Icon` and `Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, and `@calcom/ui`'s index.tsx re-exports MultiEmail (index.tsx:153). That is a circular import. It only works because the component is loaded through `next/dynamic`. No other file in packages/ui/form does this. Import from the component paths directly.

contracts.action: Add guests to a booking (tRPC addGuests mutation)
contracts.before_after: editLocation builds the evt from ctx.booking, calls EventManager.updateLocation, writes the DB only if the calendar update succeeded, and sends emails gated by event-type metadata. addGuests writes the attendees to the DB first, then calls updateCalendarAttendees and sends emails with no metadata gating.
contracts.visible_effect: onSuccess shows a toast, closes the dialog and invalidates viewer.bookings, so the list refetches and shows the new attendees.
contracts.failure_mode: updateAllCalendarEvents catches calendar errors internally, so a calendar failure is silent while the DB rows are already added. A failure while sending email is logged with console.log and the call still succeeds.

contracts.before_after: isTeamAdmin already covers OWNER. Joining it with isTeamOwner using && limits access to owners.
contracts.visible_effect: Team admins get a FORBIDDEN toast.

contracts.before_after: The sibling checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail / eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail before sending. The new function does not.
contracts.visible_effect: Emails go out even when the event type disabled standard emails.

contracts.before_after: handleNewBooking lowercases the guest and runs extractBaseEmail before comparing. The new code compares the raw guest string.
contracts.visible_effect: Blacklisted addresses that differ only in case, or that use a +alias, are added and emailed.

summary: The add-guests feature works end to end, but it has several gaps that should be fixed before merging. Team admins are blocked because the admin and owner checks are joined with `&&`. The guest blacklist and the duplicate-attendee check are case-sensitive, unlike handleNewBooking. The emails ignore the event type's disable-standard-emails settings, are keyed on the raw input instead of the guests actually added, and use APP_NAME instead of EMAIL_FROM_NAME as the sender name. In the dialog, the validation error and the typed emails survive a successful add and closing the dialog. Open question: should any attendee be able to add any number of guests?
